drug_class: Neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) blocker / monoclonal antibody
purpose: Rozanolixizumab-Noli is used to treat adults with generalized myasthenia gravis, a condition that causes muscle weakness, especially in the eyes, face, and limbs. It helps reduce the abnormal antibodies in your body that are causing your muscles to become weak. It is used specifically in patients who test positive for certain antibodies (anti-AChR or anti-MuSK).
how_it_works: Your immune system is making harmful antibodies that attack the connection between your nerves and muscles, causing weakness. This medication works by blocking a protein called FcRn, which normally recycles those harmful antibodies and keeps them in your bloodstream. By blocking FcRn, the medication helps lower the levels of those harmful antibodies so your muscles can work better.
common_side_effects: Headache (sometimes severe, including migraine-type headaches), fever, nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, rash, and fatigue. Injection site reactions like redness or swelling can also occur.
warnings: This medication can increase your risk of serious infections, including a rare but dangerous brain infection called aseptic meningitis — tell your doctor right away if you have a severe headache, stiff neck, sensitivity to light, fever, or confusion. Because it lowers protective antibodies, you may be more vulnerable to infections in general. You should be up to date on vaccinations before starting treatment. Do not use this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an infusion under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a week for 6 weeks. Your healthcare team will give it to you in a clinic setting. After 6 weeks, your doctor will evaluate whether you need additional treatment cycles.
